title: arXiv Mathematics weekly notable papers, 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-23
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper selection, and citation evidence is sparse for papers only days old. Historical replacement listings were not fully accessible, so revision-only coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove that for every fixed integer k ≥ 3, families of subsets of [n] containing no k-sunflower have size at most c_k^n for some c_k < 2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' main theorem gives an exponential upper bound with base strictly below 2 for every k ≥ 3, by bounding vector sunflowers and transferring the result to set families.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed k ≥ 3; a family is a subset of the power set of [n] and contains no k sets whose pairwise intersections all coincide.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that the best known lower construction remains close to the upper bound for large k, so the exponential base is not established as optimal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The conjecture-resolution claim is accompanied by an announced IBS seminar by coauthor Hyunwoo Lee and a public Lean formalization linked to the paper; these are engagement signals, not citation counts.

sections.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
sections.abstract: Jenia Tevelev's expository notes explain a claimed proof of Nagata's conjecture by reducing interpolation for fat points to a lattice-triangle problem, and also derive cones for certain weighted blow-ups.
sections.claimed_result: In the author's account of the OpenAI proof, for r ≥ 10 very general points of the complex projective plane, every nonzero degree-d curve vanishing to order at least m at all points satisfies d > m√r; the notes also determine nef and pseudoeffective cones for a stated class of weighted blow-ups.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Over ℂ, for r ≥ 10 very general points in P² and integer multiplicity m ≥ 1; very general means outside a countable union of proper algebraic subsets.
sections.unique_caveat: These are explicitly expository notes, not the original proof; Tevelev says they are not a definitive account and claims no originality. The underlying proof claim was not independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The preprint follows a UMass Amherst research talk on the same claim, documented by the university event page; this is attention to the claim, not proof certification.

sections.title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove a polynomial upper bound for the induced Ramsey number r_ind(G,H), at most t^(60k²+3) when G and H have k and t vertices.
sections.claimed_result: For finite simple graphs G,H with k=|V(G)| ≥ 2 and t=|V(H)| ≥ 2, the authors state r_ind(G,H) ≤ t^(60k²+3), establishing the conjectured polynomial dependence on t for fixed G.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The induced Ramsey number is the minimum order of a host graph in which every red/blue edge-colouring yields a red induced G or blue induced H; arbitrary finite simple G,H in the stated size range.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponent is large and is not claimed to be sharp; improving its dependence on k remains open-ended.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete resolution of a 1998 conjecture with an explicit bound; Wolfram MathWorld independently records the claimed polynomial bound and resolution.

sections.title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
sections.abstract: Jean-Baptiste Gouéré's short note presents an exposition of a recent proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture attributed to OpenAI.
sections.claimed_result: The paper claims to explain the proof, not to establish a new theorem; the abstract identifies the proof as one provided by OpenAI.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The abstract does not restate the conjecture's precise hypotheses; it is an expository note on a separate proof concerning percolation.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a commentary/exposition rather than the primary proof, and the abstract alone does not specify the theorem statement or permit assessment of that proof.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent discussion by Gil Kalai and a MathDB problem page describes the underlying critical-percolation claim and its relation to the conjecture; this is attention to the result, not citation momentum for this note.

sections.title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
sections.abstract: For a q-ary Griesmer code with q=p^f and e the p-adic valuation of its minimum distance, the authors claim divisibility by p^max(0,e−f+1), proving Ward's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove every [n,k,d]_q Griesmer code is p^max(0,e−f+1)-divisible when q=p^f and e=ν_p(d).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The code must attain the Griesmer bound over a finite field of characteristic p; e is the p-adic valuation of its minimum distance d.
sections.unique_caveat: The divisibility theorem is specific to Griesmer codes and does not assert the same conclusion for arbitrary linear codes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise proof claim resolves a stated conjecture and the paper is cross-listed between combinatorics and information theory; no independent discussion surfaced in the sources checked.

sections.title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
sections.abstract: For a nonconstant inner function θ, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space K_θ has a bounded symbol exactly when θ is one-component.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state the conjectured if-and-only-if characterization of when all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators on K_θ admit bounded symbols.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: θ is a nonconstant inner function; K_θ is its associated model space, and the operators are bounded truncated Toeplitz operators.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives an existence criterion for bounded symbols, not a quantitative norm-control estimate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a resolution of an operator-theory conjecture and is cross-listed in functional analysis and complex variables; MathDB documents the historical open direction.

sections.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
sections.abstract: The authors prove sharp linear upper bounds for Steklov nodal lengths and counts on smooth compact surfaces with boundary, while interior nodal length can grow beyond log λ arbitrarily slowly.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a sharp linear upper bound on interior nodal length and sharp linear bounds on boundary zeros and nodal-domain counts; interior nodal length divided by log λ tends to infinity, with examples allowing arbitrarily slow divergence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Steklov eigenfunctions on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian surface with boundary; asymptotic statements concern large eigenvalues.
sections.unique_caveat: The lower-growth conclusion is only ω(log λ), and examples rule out a universal positive-power lower bound; stronger rates require extra hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four-way mathematical cross-listing and a sharp upper bound tied to the two-dimensional Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture make this a cross-field result; independent attention signals were not found.

sections.title: Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture
sections.abstract: For even n and diverging degree d ≤ n^(1/10), a uniform random d-regular graph is asymptotically close in total variation to a union of d uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, yielding two conjecture-related consequences.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the total-variation approximation in the stated degree range, confirming the cited random-regular-graph conjecture there, and derives sprinkling and sparse-regime sandwich-conjecture consequences.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Uniform simple d-regular graphs on even n vertices; d=ω(1) and d≤n^(1/10).
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is restricted to this sparse degree window and does not address bounded d or degrees above n^(1/10).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A single theorem yields consequences for sprinkling in random regular graphs and the sparse-regime upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture; this is a concrete multi-consequence result, though no independent attention signal was found.
